title: The 10 Best Corded Chainsaws
subtitle: Plug-in electric chainsaws for firewood, limbs and storm cleanup, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A corded chainsaw starts with a trigger, never needs a charge or a gas mix, and costs less than a battery saw of the same size. We ranked 10 best-sellers from Oregon, CRAFTSMAN, BLACK+DECKER, WEN, SENIX and Makita on rating, review volume and features (an 18-inch bar, a 15 A motor, tool-free chain tensioning and automatic oiling). For battery saws, see our cordless chainsaw page.

changelog.note: Page published with 10 ranked picks and 1 tool to avoid.

products.name: Oregon CS1500 Self-Sharpening Electric Chain Saw, 18-Inch Bar, 15 Amp
products.verdict: The most-reviewed saw on this page and the only one that sharpens its own chain. Pull the PowerSharp lever for 3 to 5 seconds and the chain is back in shape without a file.
products.best_for: Homeowners who cut firewood every fall and don't want to learn to file a chain.
products.skip_if: You want a light saw for overhead pruning; it weighs 12.6 lb.

specs.extras: Low-kickback bar and chain, oil window, 3-yr warranty

products.verdict: The top result in Amazon's corded chainsaw search, with 1K+ sold last month. A 12 A, 16-inch saw with tool-free tensioning, automatic oiling and a 3-year warranty.

products.name: Oregon 2400W Corded Electric Chainsaw with 16" Guide Bar & Saw Chain

avoid.name: KAKEI 16-Inch 15-Amp Electric Chainsaw, 2200W Peak Power Corded Chain Saw with 3 German Steel Chains
avoid.flag: Wrench-only tensioning; power figures don't agree
avoid.verdict: A 16-inch saw that sells wrench-only chain tensioning as an upgrade and lists power ratings that don't agree, for more money than an 18-inch WEN with tool-free tensioning.
reasons: Chain tension needs a wrench on two hex nuts. The listing calls tool-free knobs 'fragile', but every saw on this page has tool-free or tool-less tensioning.

The title says 15 A and '2200W peak', and the spec table says 2.8 hp. A 15 A motor on a 120 V outlet draws at most 1,800 W, so the peak and horsepower figures don't describe what the motor can sustain.
The bullets say it cuts logs up to 14 inches, less than the 16-inch bar suggests.
At $84.49 it costs $4.50 more than the WEN CP1518, which has an 18 in bar, a 15 A motor and tool-free tensioning.

buyers_guide.a: A corded saw never runs out of charge and costs far less than a battery saw with a big battery. The trade is the cord: you need an outdoor extension cord and you stay within reach of an outlet. For cutting near the house or garage, corded is the cheaper choice. For the back of a large lot, see our cordless chainsaw page.

buyers_guide.q: What bar length do I need?
buyers_guide.a: A 16 in bar handles limbs and most firewood. An 18 in bar gets through bigger rounds in one pass but adds weight. Plan on cutting wood a couple of inches thinner than the bar length.

Amps are the most useful power number on a corded saw because every 120 V tool shares the same outlet limit. A 15 A saw holds its chain speed better in thick hardwood. A 12 A saw costs less and is fine for limbs and softwood.

buyers_guide.q: What extension cord should I use?
buyers_guide.a: Use an outdoor-rated cord. A thin or very long cord drops voltage and makes the motor work harder, so use the heaviest gauge your saw's manual calls for at the length you need.

buyers_guide.q: What maintenance does a corded chainsaw need?
buyers_guide.a: Keep the bar oil topped up, check chain tension before each use, and sharpen or replace the chain when it starts throwing dust instead of chips. The Oregon CS1500 sharpens its own chain.

buyers_guide.q: Why don't we compare horsepower or watts?
buyers_guide.a: Several listings print horsepower or 'peak watts' figures that a household outlet can't deliver, and they vary widely between similar saws. We show the amp rating, bar length and features instead.
